headline: 本週影評與書評
context: 紀錄片《Okurimono》記錄了長崎原爆倖存者「被爆者」（hibakusha）之間的互助網絡，導演洛朗斯．萊維斯克（Laurence Lévesque）透過女主角在整理已故母親遺物時發現的書信，帶出這些倖存者當年承受的身心創傷與社會排斥。另一本新書，是凱特．艾特金森（Kate Atkinson）的《Our Noble Selves》，故事設定在1951年英國「不列顛節」（Festival of Britain）前後，講述一名退伍戰地記者的離奇際遇。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Laurence Lévesque’s powerful documentary follows a woman who discovers a support network among her mother’s generation of survivors of the nuclear blast No words are spoken during the first five minutes of Laurence Lévesque’s documentary. In a rustic house in the city of Nagasaki, a Japanese woman in her 60s, Noriko, draws back the curtains to let in the glow of dawn. The tranquil mood, however, is deceptive. Once her childhood home, the place holds a lifetime of secrets, which Norkia only discovers after her parents’ death. While clearing out the house, she comes across letters received by her mother that shed light on her turmoil as a survivor of Nagasaki’s atomic bombing in 1945. Noriko has always known her mother was a hibakusha – a term referring to people who survived the nuclear bombs. Already scarred by psychological and physical trauma, the victims also faced ostracism in the postwar period, with many barred from work or marriage. Perhaps due to the stigma, Noriko’s mother mentioned little of this to Noriko and her siblings. The letters, however, reveal a moving network of support among the hibakusha , as well as those who lost their loved ones in the bombings. In one heartbreaking note, a grieving mother speaks of sending a healthy son into the army, only to receive his hair and clipped nails in return. Continue reading...
sources.title: Okurimono review – a heartbreaking dispatch from survivors of the Nagasaki bomb

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: There are glimpses of Atkinson’s subtle brilliance in this gentle noirish mystery set around the Festival of Britain In 1951, in a desperate attempt to raise the spirits of a shattered nation, the government came up with the Festival of Britain, a celebration of national creativity, grit and ingenuity. It is a moment in history that could have been designed for Kate Atkinson, who loves nothing more than a quirky detail and a cast of British eccentrics. Harry Flynn (definitely think Errol), the quietly magnetic hero of Our Noble Selves, has survived Burma as a foreign correspondent turned war reporter. After a doomed marriage to a war widow called Ivy, and a stint in a mock-Tudor semi in Wealdstone with her, her eight-year-old daughter Veronica and a terrier, Mrs Betty, he resumes his bachelor life in London. A chance encounter with his old newspaper boss, Gerald Barry, leads him to a job compiling the festival’s poetry anthology. Barry provides a handy introduction: “The country’s stuck in the doldrums; we need to see the future,” he explains. The festival will celebrate “the Land and the People … Our love of country, love of freedom, love of nature, pride in craftsmanship, our reputation for tolerance and fair play.” Continue reading...
sources.title: Our Noble Selves by Kate Atkinson review – quirky postwar nostalgia from the Life After Life author

thread_text:
紀錄片《Okurimono》記錄了長崎原爆倖存者「被爆者」（hibakusha）之間的互助網絡。導演洛朗斯．萊維斯克（Laurence Lévesque）透過女主角在整理已故母親遺物時發現的書信，揭露這些倖存者當年承受的身心創傷，以及戰後遭受的社會排斥。另一邊，作家凱特．艾特金森（Kate Atkinson）推出新書《Our Noble Selves》，故事設定在1951年英國「不列顛節」（Festival of Britain）前後，描寫一名退伍戰地記者的離奇際遇，帶著懷舊又略帶偵探色彩的氣氛。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian，2026 年 9 月 7 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text: 這次要介紹一部紀錄片和一本小說。紀錄片《Okurimono》，講的是長崎原爆倖存者之間的互助故事。女主角在整理已故母親的遺物時，發現了一批書信，才知道母親當年承受的身心創傷，還有戰後遭遇的社會排斥。另一本，是作家凱特．艾特金森的新書，故事設定在1951年英國「不列顛節」前後，講一名退伍戰地記者的離奇際遇，帶點懷舊、也帶點偵探小說的氣氛。
